absolute-paths-allowed-crates.description: Which crates to allow absolute paths from

absolute-paths-max-segments.description:
The maximum number of segments a path can have before being linted, anything above this will
be linted.

accept-comment-above-attributes.description: Whether to accept a safety comment to be placed above the attributes for the `unsafe` block

accept-comment-above-statement.description: Whether to accept a safety comment to be placed above the statement containing the `unsafe` block

allow-comparison-to-zero.description: Don't lint when comparing the result of a modulo operation to zero.

allow-dbg-in-tests.description: Whether `dbg!` should be allowed in test functions or `#[cfg(test)]`

allow-exact-repetitions.description: Whether an item should be allowed to have the same name as its containing module

allow-expect-in-consts.description: Whether `expect` should be allowed in code always evaluated at compile time

allow-expect-in-tests.description: Whether `expect` should be allowed in test functions or `#[cfg(test)]`

allow-indexing-slicing-in-tests.description: Whether `indexing_slicing` should be allowed in test functions or `#[cfg(test)]`

allow-large-stack-frames-in-tests.description: Whether functions inside `#[cfg(test)]` modules or test functions should be checked.

allow-mixed-uninlined-format-args.description: Whether to allow mixed uninlined format args, e.g. `format!("{} {}", a, foo.bar)`

allow-one-hash-in-raw-strings.description: Whether to allow `r#""#` when `r""` can be used

allow-panic-in-tests.description: Whether `panic` should be allowed in test functions or `#[cfg(test)]`

allow-print-in-tests.description: Whether print macros (ex. `println!`) should be allowed in test functions or `#[cfg(test)]`

allow-private-module-inception.description: Whether to allow module inception if it's not public.

allow-renamed-params-for.description:
List of trait paths to ignore when checking renamed function parameters.

#### Example

```toml
allow-renamed-params-for = [ "std::convert::From" ]
```

#### Noteworthy

- By default, the following traits are ignored: `From`, `TryFrom`, `FromStr`
- `".."` can be used as part of the list to indicate that the configured values should be appended to the
default configuration of Clippy. By default, any configuration will replace the default value.

allow-unwrap-in-consts.description: Whether `unwrap` should be allowed in code always evaluated at compile time

allow-unwrap-in-tests.description: Whether `unwrap` should be allowed in test functions or `#[cfg(test)]`

allow-unwrap-types.description:
List of types to allow `unwrap()` and `expect()` on.

#### Example

```toml
allow-unwrap-types = [ "std::sync::LockResult" ]
```

allow-useless-vec-in-tests.description: Whether `useless_vec` should ignore test functions or `#[cfg(test)]`

allowed-dotfiles.description: Additional dotfiles (files or directories starting with a dot) to allow

allowed-duplicate-crates.description: A list of crate names to allow duplicates of

allowed-idents-below-min-chars.description:
Allowed names below the minimum allowed characters. The value `".."` can be used as part of
the list to indicate that the configured values should be appended to the default
configuration of Clippy. By default, any configuration will replace the default value.

allowed-prefixes.description:
List of prefixes to allow when determining whether an item's name ends with the module's name.
If the rest of an item's name is an allowed prefix (e.g. item `ToFoo` or `to_foo` in module `foo`),
then don't emit a warning.

#### Example

```toml
allowed-prefixes = [ "to", "from" ]
```

#### Noteworthy

- By default, the following prefixes are allowed: `to`, `as`, `into`, `from`, `try_into` and `try_from`
- PascalCase variant is included automatically for each snake_case variant (e.g. if `try_into` is included,
  `TryInto` will also be included)
- Use `".."` as part of the list to indicate that the configured values should be appended to the
default configuration of Clippy. By default, any configuration will replace the default value

allowed-scripts.description: The list of unicode scripts allowed to be used in the scope.

allowed-wildcard-imports.description:
List of path segments allowed to have wildcard imports.

#### Example

```toml
allowed-wildcard-imports = [ "utils", "common" ]
```

#### Noteworthy

1. This configuration has no effects if used with `warn_on_all_wildcard_imports = true`.
2. Paths with any segment that containing the word 'prelude'
are already allowed by default.

arithmetic-side-effects-allowed.description:
Suppress checking of the passed type names in all types of operations.

If a specific operation is desired, consider using `arithmetic_side_effects_allowed_binary` or `arithmetic_side_effects_allowed_unary` instead.

#### Example

```toml
arithmetic-side-effects-allowed = ["SomeType", "AnotherType"]
```

#### Noteworthy

A type, say `SomeType`, listed in this configuration has the same behavior of
`["SomeType" , "*"], ["*", "SomeType"]` in `arithmetic_side_effects_allowed_binary`.

arithmetic-side-effects-allowed-binary.description:
Suppress checking of the passed type pair names in binary operations like addition or
multiplication.

Supports the "*" wildcard to indicate that a certain type won't trigger the lint regardless
of the involved counterpart. For example, `["SomeType", "*"]` or `["*", "AnotherType"]`.

Pairs are asymmetric, which means that `["SomeType", "AnotherType"]` is not the same as
`["AnotherType", "SomeType"]`.

#### Example

```toml
arithmetic-side-effects-allowed-binary = [["SomeType" , "f32"], ["AnotherType", "*"]]
```

arithmetic-side-effects-allowed-unary.description:
Suppress checking of the passed type names in unary operations like "negation" (`-`).

#### Example

```toml
arithmetic-side-effects-allowed-unary = ["SomeType", "AnotherType"]
```

array-size-threshold.description: The maximum allowed size for arrays on the stack

avoid-breaking-exported-api.description: Suppress lints whenever the suggested change would cause breakage for other crates.

await-holding-invalid-types.description: The list of types which may not be held across an await point.

blacklisted-names.description:
Deprecated. Use `disallowed-names` instead.

The list of disallowed names to lint about. NB: `bar` is not here since it has legitimate uses. The value
`".."` can be used as part of the list to indicate that the configured values should be appended to the
default configuration of Clippy. By default, any configuration will replace the default value.

cargo-ignore-publish.description: For internal testing only, ignores the current `publish` settings in the Cargo manifest.

check-incompatible-msrv-in-tests.description: Whether to check MSRV compatibility in `#[test]` and `#[cfg(test)]` code.

check-private-items.description: Whether to also run the listed lints on private items.

cognitive-complexity-threshold.description: The maximum cognitive complexity a function can have

const-literal-digits-threshold.description: The minimum digits a const float literal must have to suppress the `excessive_precision` lint

cyclomatic-complexity-threshold.description:
Deprecated. Use `cognitive-complexity-threshold` instead.

The maximum cognitive complexity a function can have

disallowed-fields.description:
The list of disallowed fields, written as fully qualified paths.

**Fields:**
- `path` (required): the fully qualified path to the field that should be disallowed
- `reason` (optional): explanation why this field is disallowed
- `replacement` (optional): suggested alternative method
- `allow-invalid` (optional, `false` by default): when set to `true`, it will ignore this entry
  if the path doesn't exist, instead of emitting an error

disallowed-macros.description:
The list of disallowed macros, written as fully qualified paths.

**Fields:**
- `path` (required): the fully qualified path to the macro that should be disallowed
- `reason` (optional): explanation why this macro is disallowed
- `replacement` (optional): suggested alternative macro
- `allow-invalid` (optional, `false` by default): when set to `true`, it will ignore this entry
  if the path doesn't exist, instead of emitting an error

disallowed-methods.description:
The list of disallowed methods, written as fully qualified paths.

**Fields:**
- `path` (required): the fully qualified path to the method that should be disallowed
- `reason` (optional): explanation why this method is disallowed
- `replacement` (optional): suggested alternative method
- `allow-invalid` (optional, `false` by default): when set to `true`, it will ignore this entry
  if the path doesn't exist, instead of emitting an error

disallowed-names.description:
The list of disallowed names to lint about. NB: `bar` is not here since it has legitimate uses. The value
`".."` can be used as part of the list to indicate that the configured values should be appended to the
default configuration of Clippy. By default, any configuration will replace the default value.

disallowed-types.description:
The list of disallowed types, written as fully qualified paths.

**Fields:**
- `path` (required): the fully qualified path to the type that should be disallowed
- `reason` (optional): explanation why this type is disallowed
- `replacement` (optional): suggested alternative type
- `allow-invalid` (optional, `false` by default): when set to `true`, it will ignore this entry
  if the path doesn't exist, instead of emitting an error

doc-valid-idents.description:
The list of words this lint should not consider as identifiers needing ticks. The value
`".."` can be used as part of the list to indicate that the configured values should be appended to the
default configuration of Clippy. By default, any configuration will replace the default value. For example:
* `doc-valid-idents = ["ClipPy"]` would replace the default list with `["ClipPy"]`.
* `doc-valid-idents = ["ClipPy", ".."]` would append `ClipPy` to the default list.

enable-raw-pointer-heuristic-for-send.description: Whether to apply the raw pointer heuristic to determine if a type is `Send`.

enforced-import-renames.description: The list of imports to always rename, a fully qualified path followed by the rename.

enum-variant-name-threshold.description: The minimum number of enum variants for the lints about variant names to trigger

enum-variant-size-threshold.description: The maximum size of an enum's variant to avoid box suggestion

excessive-nesting-threshold.description: The maximum amount of nesting a block can reside in

future-size-threshold.description: The maximum byte size a `Future` can have, before it triggers the `clippy::large_futures` lint

ignore-interior-mutability.description: A list of paths to types that should be treated as if they do not contain interior mutability

inherent-impl-lint-scope.description: Sets the scope ("crate", "file", or "module") in which duplicate inherent `impl` blocks for the same type are linted.

large-error-ignored.description:
A list of paths to types that should be ignored as overly large `Err`-variants in a
`Result` returned from a function

large-error-threshold.description: The maximum size of the `Err`-variant in a `Result` returned from a function

lint-commented-code.description:
Whether collapsible `if` and `else if` chains are linted if they contain comments inside the parts
that would be collapsed.

literal-representation-threshold.description: The lower bound for linting decimal literals

matches-for-let-else.description:
Whether the matches should be considered by the lint, and whether there should
be filtering for common types.

max-fn-params-bools.description:
The maximum number of bool parameters a function can have.
Use `0` to lint on any function with a bool parameter.

max-include-file-size.description: The maximum size of a file included via `include_bytes!()` or `include_str!()`, in bytes

max-struct-bools.description: The maximum number of bool fields a struct can have

max-suggested-slice-pattern-length.description:
When Clippy suggests using a slice pattern, this is the maximum number of elements allowed in
the slice pattern that is suggested. If more elements are necessary, the lint is suppressed.
For example, `[_, _, _, e, ..]` is a slice pattern with 4 elements.

max-trait-bounds.description: The maximum number of bounds a trait can have to be linted

may-panic-functions.description:
List of function/method paths that may panic and should be documented with a `// Panic:` comment
at call sites.

min-ident-chars-lint-trait-impl.description: Whether to lint idents that have too few chars even when following trait declaration.

min-ident-chars-threshold.description: Minimum chars an ident can have, anything below or equal to this will be linted.

missing-docs-allow-unused.description: Whether to allow fields starting with an underscore to skip documentation requirements

missing-docs-in-crate-items.description:
Whether to **only** check for missing documentation in items visible within the current
crate. For example, `pub(crate)` items.

module-item-order-groupings.description: The named groupings of different source item kinds within modules.

module-items-ordered-within-groupings.description:
Whether the items within module groups should be ordered alphabetically or not.

This option can be configured to "all", "none", or a list of specific grouping names that should be checked
(e.g. only "enums").

msrv.description: The minimum rust version that the project supports. Defaults to the `rust-version` field in `Cargo.toml`

pass-by-value-size-limit.description: The minimum size (in bytes) to consider a type for passing by reference instead of by value.

pub-underscore-fields-behavior.description:
Lint "public" fields in a struct that are prefixed with an underscore based on their
exported visibility, or whether they are marked as "pub".

recursive-self-in-type-definitions.description: Whether the type itself in a struct or enum should be replaced with `Self` when encountering recursive types.

semicolon-inside-block-ignore-singleline.description: Whether to lint only if it's multiline.

semicolon-outside-block-ignore-multiline.description: Whether to lint only if it's singleline.

single-char-binding-names-threshold.description: The maximum number of single char bindings a scope may have

source-item-ordering.description: Which kind of elements should be ordered internally, possible values being `enum`, `impl`, `module`, `struct`, `trait`.

stack-size-threshold.description: The maximum allowed stack size for functions in bytes

standard-macro-braces.description:
Enforce the named macros always use the braces specified.

A `MacroMatcher` can be added like so `{ name = "macro_name", brace = "(" }`. If the macro
could be used with a full path two `MacroMatcher`s have to be added one with the full path
`crate_name::macro_name` and one with just the macro name.

struct-field-name-threshold.description: The minimum number of struct fields for the lints about field names to trigger

suppress-restriction-lint-in-const.description:
Whether to suppress a restriction lint in constant code. In same
cases the restructured operation might not be unavoidable, as the
suggested counterparts are unavailable in constant code. This
configuration will cause restriction lints to trigger even
if no suggestion can be made.

third-party.description: Third-party configuration. Clippy ignores the value of this setting.

too-large-for-stack.description: The maximum size of objects (in bytes) that will be linted. Larger objects are ok on the heap

too-many-arguments-threshold.description: The maximum number of argument a function or method can have

too-many-lines-threshold.description: The maximum number of lines a function or method can have

trait-assoc-item-kinds-order.description: The order of associated items in traits.

trait-impl-item-order.description:
The required ordering of associated items in trait impls: purely alphabetical,
following the trait definition order, or accepting either.

Note that the trait definition order may change between versions of the
crate defining the trait without being considered a breaking change.

Examples:
When using trait definition item ordering:
```toml
trait-impl-item-order = "trait_item_ordering"
```
When using trait definition item ordering and alphabetical for fallbacks:
```toml
trait-impl-item-order = "alphabetical_or_trait_item_ordering"
```

trivial-copy-size-limit.description:
The maximum size (in bytes) to consider a `Copy` type for passing by value instead of by
reference.

type-complexity-threshold.description: The maximum complexity a type can have

unnecessary-box-size.description: The byte size a `T` in `Box<T>` can have, below which it triggers the `clippy::unnecessary_box` lint

unreadable-literal-lint-fractions.description: Should the fraction of a decimal be linted to include separators.

upper-case-acronyms-aggressive.description: Enables verbose mode. Triggers if there is more than one uppercase char next to each other

vec-box-size-threshold.description: The size of the boxed type in bytes, where boxing in a `Vec` is allowed

verbose-bit-mask-threshold.description: The maximum allowed size of a bit mask before suggesting to use 'trailing_zeros'

warn-on-all-wildcard-imports.description:
Whether to emit warnings on all wildcard imports, including those from `prelude`, from `super` in tests,
or for `pub use` reexports.

warn-unsafe-macro-metavars-in-private-ma.description: Whether to also emit warnings for unsafe blocks with metavariable expansions in **private** macros.
